steps.text: Preheat oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Mix together the ketchup, cola and brown sugar.
Place pork chops into a baking pan and pour cola mixture over, coating well. Sprinkle with salt and pepper.
Bake for about one hour depending on the thickness of the pork chop.

raw_recipe.headline: Cola Pork Chops
raw_recipe.description: This is a tried and true recipe for pork chops, but it works great using chicken too. With chicken, cooking time is more like 40 minutes for thick breasts.
raw_recipe.name: Cola Pork Chops

review.reviewBody: I have been making this for years and have never had any negetive feedback.I roll my chops in flour and brown them before baking,not only does this make a much jucier chop,it also helps to thicken the sauce.

I made this in a pressure cooker and it turned out very moist and flavorful. Cooked for 12 min, turn off, let pressure drop and served. I used full can of Coke (12oz) and 12 Oz of ketchup for 4 bone in pork chops.

Season, flour, brown first. Place six 1 inch cuts into 9x13 pan. Pour the cola, ketchup, brown sugar sauce over it. Cover with foil .Cook 35 minutes at 350-375 F. Remove foil. Let rest 5 minutes. Very moist and tender. Nice flavor. I added some chili powder and salt to cut the sweetness and give it another layer of flavor. My pickiest eater liked it.
Good recipe but I cook it in my crock pot on low for about 4 hours and the meat falls off the bone. I also add some Sweet Baby Rays BBQ sauce to it as well turns out so so good.

Excellent way to make chops. They come out so tender. I did 1/2 cup ketchup and 1/2 barbeque sauce instead of just ketchup. And, like other reviewers, I coated them in flour (seasoned with salt, pepper, onion powder, & garlic powder) and browned them first. I did find that most of the sauce burned off in the pan. I would definitely recommend coating the chops with only 1/2 of the cola mixture for the first half hour of baking. That's plenty to coat the top of the chops. Let it go about 30 minutes, take the pan out of the oven, flip the chops, then add the rest of the mixture. You'll end up with "saucier" chops in the end. Other than that though, no complaints. The sauce gave them a really good barbequed flavor. It was almost like eating some good ribs.

Very good recipe nice change to the normal pork chop recipes. Tangy and moist I took some changes from other reviews to incorporate into my dinner tonight pan flash fried the pork chops before I baked them with flour salt pepper and paprika. Then before I poured the sauce over them in the baking pan I placed butter in between a few then poured the sauce and salt n peppered on top. They came out juciy and moist so yummy. Will try with chicken next time. :) once you try this easy recipe you won't regret you did!

I have to admit I was skeptical about this one..but after reading the reviews I decided to give it a try. So glad I did!! I rolled in flour, seasoned with garlic, onion, salt and pepper, then browned them before baking in the sauce for 30 minutes.....and it was FANTASTIC! Thank you!

Yum! There were so many good suggestions from all the reviews. I chose to make the following changes. I seasoned and browned the pork first. I didn't have enought katchup, so I substituted Banana Katchup (from the Asian market, and a staple in Filipino kitchens). I mixed the sauce ingredients together before pouring over chops. I added 2 tablespoon of onion soup mix to the cola mixture. It was SOOO flavorful! I will make this again, but next time I will try it in the slow cooker.

Loved this with a few minor changes. Like many others, I salted and dusted my chops with flour and browned them a few minutes first. I used Pepsi since it is what I had on hand. Instead of getting another dish dirty, I added the sauce to my skillet on the stove. I covered it up and turned it down to a low simmer and cooked half an hour or so. Served with white rice. This really reminded me of sweet and sour pork. I am making this again soon and I am going to try cutting the pork into smaller pieces before cooking to see how that works. It was just slightly messy to be trying to cut up the pork chop while it was sliding around on the rice in all that sauce.

My friends love this recipe! I used egg wash, flour and panko bread crumbs. Fried them in peanut oil. Placed them on a rack to drain. I cooked the sauce ingredients on the stove top to thicken it, covered the chops and baked until done. Served with tossed salad and baked mac. We are having it again tomorrow night.
Used suggestions from reviews, dredged chops in flour and browned before putting in casserole with sauce.
Was good, will make again

Loving it, except I used the coke like a brine and did not add any sugar. Why I never though of soda as a brine or for flavor, I don't know. The acid tenderizes meat and I will try this with chicken or beef.
I liked the recipe as is but my son said it was too sweet. Next time I will do as others suggested and use 1/2 ketchp and 1/2 bbq sauce.
I made it just the way the recipe was written. It was great and there was nothing left for left overs.

I'm afraid there was just nothing special about this BBQ sauce. I would have been just as happy to use bottled sauce and saved the time. It was very runny, so I would recommend less cola. Next time I'll search elsewhere for a cola BBQ sauce. On the plus side, the meat was tender.
I brown off my pork chops. I also use 1/2 ketcup and 1/2 bbq sauce. I heat up the liquid and add a little cornstarch to thicken. A great recipe to take and make it your own.

I followed other reviewers and browned the pork chops with seasoned flour of garlic powder, a shake of crazy salt and a bit of black pepper. I also used 1/2 BBQ sauce with the ketchup because I had one opened. I only had 2 think boneless pork chops so I reduced the amounts of ketchup and BBQ sauce to what I thought I would use. I baked them about 30 minutes. I kept the left over sauce and used it for dipping! Yummy!
this was a very dry, overcooked pork chop, and I even took it out of the oven early. I won't make it again
This recipe is similar to Filipino BBQ recipes I have seen and used in the past.
